mesure.affichage.reserve_hors_ligne: This figure comes from the training trials: only "Guided test" tells you what the mode really does.
mesure.alpha.briefing.1: This is a GATE: if this check fails, no other test in the session makes sense. Then fix the setup, not the next test.
mesure.alpha.briefing.2: Sequence: headset settling, then {duree} s eyes open, then {duree} s eyes closed.
mesure.alpha.briefing.3: A beep announces each change. It is essential: half of the measure is done with your eyes closed, so you cannot see anything.
mesure.alpha.briefing.4: Stay still, jaw relaxed: clenching your teeth drowns alpha under muscle noise.
mesure.alpha.briefing.5: Eyes open: look at a point in front of you, and blink as little as possible.
mesure.alpha.briefing.6: Eyes closed: keep them closed until the next beep, without squeezing your eyelids.
mesure.alpha.chiffres: Alpha is {ratio} times stronger with eyes closed (reference > {repere}), with a peak at {pic} Hz.
mesure.alpha.consigne.ouvert: Eyes open: look at a point in front of you
mesure.alpha.consigne.prep_ferme: Close your eyes at the next beep
mesure.alpha.consigne.prep_ouvert: Eyes open: we start in a moment
mesure.alpha.erreur.phase_manquante: missing phase(s): {phases}. The ratio needs both phases: with only one, there would be nothing to compare.
mesure.alpha.erreur.voies_plates: the {n} occipital channels ({voies}) are flat during "{etape}" (signal level: {sigmas} µV, below the dead-channel threshold of {seuil} µV). This is not a result but a connection fault: cable, electrodes, or headset switched off.
mesure.alpha.honnetete:
This check says one thing only: alpha on the occipital channels rises when you close your eyes. So the electrodes touch, the reference holds, and the channel order is right. It predicts nothing: neither the accuracy of the SSVEP nor that of a model-based mode. It either passes or it does not: a ratio of 6 is no better than a ratio of 2.
The reference "ratio > {repere}" comes from one single person, on this headset: an order of magnitude, not a validated threshold. Alpha varies a lot from one person to another.
mesure.alpha.label: Check the headset
mesure.alpha.rappel.ferme: a beep will say when to open them. Until then, you cannot see anything: that is normal.
mesure.alpha.rappel.ouvert: still, blink as little as possible
mesure.alpha.rappel.prep_ferme: and keep them closed until the next beep
mesure.alpha.rappel.prep_ouvert: settle in, stay still. A beep will announce the start.
mesure.alpha.reserve.hors_bande: It rises, but outside the alpha band: probably a movement. Do it again, still, jaw relaxed.
mesure.alpha.reserve.ne_monte_pas: Alpha does not rise: check the occipital electrodes and the mastoids, add salt water, then run it again. Nothing else is worth doing before that.
mesure.alpha.reserve.net: The headset is well placed: the session can start.
mesure.alpha.summary: Eyes open, then eyes closed: do the occipital electrodes pick up alpha? Do this first, everything else depends on it.
mesure.alpha.verdict.hors_bande: {mot}. Something rises when you close your eyes (ratio {ratio}), but the peak falls at {pic} Hz, outside the alpha range ({bas}-{haut} Hz): probably a slow drift or a movement, not alpha. Check the occipital electrodes ({voies}) and the mastoids, then do the check again, still, jaw relaxed.
mesure.alpha.verdict.ne_monte_pas: {mot}. Alpha does not rise when you close your eyes: ratio {ratio} for a reference of {repere}. Until this is fixed, no other test in the session makes sense: they all read this signal. Fix it in order: 1) do the occipital electrodes ({voies}) touch the scalp, with the hair parted? 2) do the mastoids (the reference) hold? 3) add salt water to the electrodes: that is the most effective move on this headset. Also check that your eyes were closed and that you did not move, then run it again.
mesure.alpha.verdict.net: {mot} with eyes closed: ratio {ratio} (reference > {repere}), peak at {pic} Hz on {voies}. The occipital electrodes touch, the reference holds, the channel order is right: the session can start.
mesure.commun.modele_requis: A trained model is needed: it decides. A test writes nothing to disk: it gives a score, not a model.
mesure.commun.sans_acquisition: no acquisition: it is impossible to cut the signal the way the mode does, so impossible to measure what it does.
mesure.cvep_test.briefing.1: This test replays the training, but the engine decides instead of learning: at the end of each block, it says which target it sees, and we compare with the circled target.
mesure.cvep_test.briefing.muet: The engine often stays silent, and that is normal: a block with no answer is not an error, it only lowers the share of blocks where the engine answers. Read both numbers together.
mesure.cvep_test.chiffres: Target detected in {emis} blocks out of {n} ({taux}); no answer in the other {muets}. Of these {emis} detections, the right target {justes} times: {justesse} (chance: {hasard}).
mesure.cvep_test.chiffres.sans_horloge: no decision possible: the code clock was used in none of the {n} blocks
mesure.cvep_test.erreur.trop_peu: {n} block(s) kept: not enough to conclude, the likely range would be too wide.
mesure.cvep_test.honnetete:
One decision per block: this is what your app would have received at the end of the block. The mode outputs {cadence} decisions per second on overlapping windows: counting them as trials would give too narrow a range, so misleading.
A block with no answer is never an error: it only counts in the share of blocks where the engine answers. Read both numbers together: "71% correct answers" without "46% of blocks with an answer" describes a system you do not have.
It is this reference (computed offline, on one session) that you should compare with this test, not the 59.5 / 64.9% of training, which is measured without thresholds or vote.
At most {blocs} blocks per test: the range stays wide. This reference comes from one person only: expect less. This score describes this session.
mesure.cvep_test.label: Test the c-VEP
mesure.cvep_test.param.essais.aide: The number of recorded cycles for each target, split into at most {blocs} blocks per target, shuffled across targets. The test gives one decision per block: {durees}. Beyond {max}, the blocks get longer without there being more of them: the test takes longer without one more decision.
mesure.cvep_test.param.essais.label: Length: recorded cycles per target
mesure.cvep_test.perte.en_chauffe: {n} block(s) played while the headset was settling
mesure.cvep_test.perte.perdus: {n} block(s) played without usable signal (the signal had left the engine's memory)
mesure.cvep_test.rappel: look at the circled disc without moving your eyes: the engine decides at the end of each block
mesure.cvep_test.reserve.bavard: It often answers, but gets {erreurs} of its answers wrong (reference: about {repere}): raise "{seuil}" or "{marge}" one notch, then test again.
mesure.cvep_test.reserve.bon: Measured on {n} blocks of this session: the range stays wide. Test again after a break before taking these settings into your app.
mesure.cvep_test.reserve.faible: Not distinguishable from chance ({p}): train again. Put salt water back on Pz/PO7/Oz/PO8, and keep your gaze on the circled disc.
mesure.cvep_test.reserve.faible_court: Not distinguishable from chance ({p}): with {emis} blocks decided, we cannot conclude. Redo the test at {long} cycles per target ({blocs} blocks) before judging.
mesure.cvep_test.reserve.horloge_perdue: The code clock was lost on most blocks: the stimulus window must stay open, without interruption, until the end.
mesure.cvep_test.reserve.horloge_refusee: The mode refused the window's clock ({refus}): train again on this screen.
mesure.cvep_test.reserve.moyen: Below the reference on both numbers: put salt water back on Pz/PO7/Oz/PO8, and train again before touching the thresholds.
mesure.cvep_test.reserve.sans_cycle: No usable "cycle" marker: the stimulus window must stay open until the end. Do not close it, do not send it to the background.
mesure.cvep_test.reserve.seuils: No block passes the thresholds: put salt water back on Pz/PO7/Oz/PO8, then lower "{seuil}" one notch and test again.
mesure.cvep_test.reserve.silencieux: Right when it answers, but it only answers on {taux} of the blocks (reference: about {repere}): lower "{seuil}" or "{vote}" one notch, then test again.
mesure.cvep_test.reserve.vote: The windows never agree: keep your gaze on the circled disc, or lower "{vote}", then test again.
mesure.cvep_test.summary: The training replayed: the engine decides block by block with your model and your settings, and we compare with the circled target.
mesure.cvep_test.verdict.base: {mot} — over {n} blocks (one decision per block, at the end of the block, never one per window),
mesure.cvep_test.verdict.ecarts: Your settings differ from those of the reference ({liste}): the comparison is only indicative.
mesure.cvep_test.verdict.emis: the engine named a target {emis} times, that is {taux} of the blocks (likely range: {em_bas} to {em_haut} %). It was right {justes} times out of {emis}, that is {justesse} correct answers (likely range: {bas} to {haut} %), for a chance level of {hasard} ({k} targets). Chance probability of such a score on the decided blocks: {p} — {conclusion}.
mesure.cvep_test.verdict.muet: the engine named no target ({taux} of the blocks), for a chance level of {hasard} ({k} targets).
mesure.cvep_test.verdict.pertes: ⚠️ Left out of the calculation: {liste}. The calculation covers {n} blocks, no more.
mesure.cvep_test.verdict.repere: Live reference, at the mode's default settings: about {emission} of the blocks with an answer and about {justesse} correct answers (computed offline, per voted window, on one session). This is not the 59.5 / 64.9% of training, which is measured without thresholds or vote.
mesure.cvep_test.verdict.silences: The {n} block(s) with no answer (-1) do not count as errors: {liste}.
mesure.errp_test.briefing.1: This test replays the training, but the engine decides instead of learning: at each step, it says whether it saw an error. We compare with the errors the window makes on purpose.
mesure.errp_test.briefing.modele: You need a trained model: it makes the decisions, with your setting "{reglage}". A test writes nothing to disk: it gives a score, not a model.
mesure.errp_test.briefing.repos: At the start, the track stays still for a few seconds: do not move, the engine measures your resting noise level.
mesure.errp_test.chiffres: {tnr} of the correct commands kept, {tpr} of the errors caught (chance: {fpr}, as many as it cancels) · {erreurs} errors out of {verdicts} verdicts
mesure.errp_test.conseil.rejet: Almost no step received a verdict: check the contact of Fz/Cz/Pz, blink less when the dot moves, then test again.
mesure.errp_test.consigne.repos: Look at the still track, without moving: the engine measures your resting noise level.
mesure.errp_test.erreur.repos_court: rest too short: the resting noise level was measured over only {duree} s, instead of the mode's {mode} s, because the window started its steps too early. No conclusion: with so little measurement, the artifact rejection threshold triggers at the slightest blink, and the test would catch errors the mode will not catch. Restart "Guided test" without touching the window: it waits for the end of the rest by itself.
mesure.errp_test.erreur.sans_etiquette: no trial scored: {n} steps with no readable error indication. Was the window launched by "Guided test"?
mesure.errp_test.erreur.sans_feedback: no step received during the trials: nothing to score.
mesure.errp_test.erreur.vide: no step scored: nothing to measure.
mesure.errp_test.erreur.voie_morte: the resting noise level (used to reject artifacts) could not be measured: one channel is perfectly flat (electrode off, cable, amplifier saturated). The mode would refuse to decode like this, and so would the test. Check the contact, then restart the test.
mesure.errp_test.honnetete:
One decision per step, on new trials, with your model and the threshold the engine derives from "{reglage}". The answer of each step is used only for scoring: the decoder never sees it.
A step with no verdict (artifact, or a second of lost signal) counts separately: neither an error caught nor a correct command kept.
There is no single chance level: this is a detector, not a choice between several targets. By chance, it would catch as many errors as it cancels correct commands; a statistical test (Fisher, p-value) tells whether the gap exceeds the noise.
Reference: {tpr} of errors caught for {tnr} of correct commands kept (in one person). These rates are optimistic, because the threshold was chosen on the same scores that measure them: expect to keep fewer correct commands than aimed. Out of about ten errors, catching five is expected; eight or two stay within the noise.
The resting noise level is measured over 8 s of stillness, before the first step. If this rest is cut short, the test is cancelled: the rejection threshold would be skewed, and the test would catch errors the mode will not catch.
mesure.errp_test.label: Test the ErrP
mesure.errp_test.param.essais.aide: Steps of the track, with one verdict per step. The default is short, because this test is redone at each setting. But errors caught are counted on the deliberate errors only (~{taux} of the steps): {durees}. {max} is the length of the training: use this value to decide.
mesure.errp_test.param.essais.label: Trials
mesure.errp_test.raison.sans_bonne: no correct command judged over {n} steps
mesure.errp_test.rappel.repos: do not blink now: we measure the resting noise, which is used to reject artifacts
mesure.errp_test.reserve.bon: Measured on new trials of this session: test again after a break before taking this setting into your app.
mesure.errp_test.reserve.extreme: The reference is taken at "{reglage}" = {defaut}; at {vise}, even a good detector separates less well: test again at {defaut} before retraining.
mesure.errp_test.reserve.faible_court: With {erreurs} errors judged, we cannot tell this detector from chance: redo the test with {long} trials before judging.
mesure.errp_test.reserve.faible_long: Indistinguishable from chance, even on a long test: train again. Put salt water back on Fz, Cz and Pz, and do not anticipate the errors.
mesure.errp_test.reserve.garde_peu: It keeps fewer correct commands than asked ({tnr} for {vise}): the training threshold is optimistic. Raise "{reglage}", then test again.
mesure.errp_test.reserve.rejet: {taux} of the steps with no verdict (artifact, second of lost signal): blink less when the dot moves, check the contact, then test again.
mesure.errp_test.reserve.sous_repere: Better than chance, but worse than the reference: train again (put salt water back on Fz, Cz and Pz, do not anticipate). Moving "{reglage}" trades one rate against the other, without gaining anything.
mesure.errp_test.sans_verdict: {n} without verdict (-1: {artefacts} artifact(s), {perdus} second(s) of lost signal) count separately: neither an error caught nor a correct command kept
mesure.errp_test.summary: The training replayed: the engine decides with your model and your setting, and we compare with the errors the window makes on purpose.
mesure.errp_test.verdict.base: {mot} — over {n} steps (one step = one decision), the engine judged {jugees}; {sans}. Among the {bonnes} correct commands judged, it kept {gardees}, that is {tnr} (likely range: {tnr_bas} to {tnr_haut} %) for {vise} aimed at. Among the {erreurs} deliberate errors judged, it caught {attrapees}, that is {tpr} (likely range: {tpr_bas} to {tpr_haut} %). By chance, it would catch as many errors as it cancels correct commands ({fpr}). Chance probability of such a gap: {p} — {conclusion}.
mesure.errp_test.verdict.chauffe: {n} step(s) received during the headset settling were discarded.
mesure.errp_test.verdict.non_mesure: {mot} — {raison}: without a trial, no rate is possible; {sans}.
mesure.errp_test.verdict.promesse: On its own calibration, this model promised {tnr} of correct commands kept and {tpr} of errors caught at this setting: optimistic rates, since measured on the scores used to choose the threshold.
mesure.errp_test.verdict.repere: Reference (setting {defaut}, in one person): {tpr} caught for {tnr} kept, a gap of {ecart} points; here {ici}.
mesure.errp_test.verdict.repos: Resting noise level (used to reject artifacts): measured over {secondes} s of still track{fenetres}, like the mode ({mode} s).
mesure.fenetre.abandon.sans_annonce: the stimulus window did not announce itself ("calib_start") within {attente} s: it did not launch, or it publishes under a name other than "{flux}".
mesure.fenetre.abandon.silence: the stimulus window has not responded for {silence} s, in the middle of the session: {vus} trial(s) received out of {annonces} announced, of which {retenus} recorded. No verdict: a score computed on an interrupted session would look like a complete one.
mesure.fenetre.chauffe: The headset is settling: the stimulus window takes over in a moment.
mesure.fenetre.essais: The session runs in the stimulus window: follow its cues.
mesure.mi_test.briefing.1: This test replays the training, but this time the model answers: at the end of each trial, it says which task it recognizes, and we compare with the cue.
mesure.mi_test.briefing.2: Sequence: the headset settles ({chauffe} s), then the trials come in a random order: {pause} s of break, the cue, the lead-in chosen in training, then {imagerie} s of imagery.
mesure.mi_test.briefing.3: A beep marks the start and the end of each trial, and the cue is written on screen.
mesure.mi_test.briefing.4: Imagine exactly as in training: as soon as the cue appears, feel the movement, without moving, until the break. REST = imagine nothing.
mesure.mi_test.chiffres: The model answered in {emis} trials out of {n} (no answer in the other {muets}). Of these {emis} answers, the right task {justes} times: {justesse} (chance: {hasard}).
mesure.mi_test.chiffres.muet: no answer over {n} trials (chance: {hasard}): the model was never sure enough
mesure.mi_test.consigne.pause: Break: relax, the next trial is coming
mesure.mi_test.erreur.sans_fenetre: a trial of {duree} s is shorter than a window of {fenetre} s: the test and the decoding are no longer set the same way.
mesure.mi_test.erreur.trop_peu: {n} trial(s) only: too few to conclude.
mesure.mi_test.honnetete:
One answer per trial: the one your app would have received at the end of the trial. The {fenetres} windows of a trial do not count as that many trials: that would make the result look ~{facteur} times more precise than it is.
A trial with no answer counts in "the model answered in…", never as an error nor as REST: REST is a task the model must recognize, "I don't know" is not one.
For comparison: on this headset, in one person, we got 63% with two tasks (fists) and 40% with three (adding rest), in training. The score drops with fatigue: it describes this session.
mesure.mi_test.label: Test the Motor Imagery
mesure.mi_test.param.essais.aide: Short by default, so you can redo this test at each setting. If the result says we cannot conclude, use {long} trials per task to decide. Durations with 3 tasks: {durees}.
mesure.mi_test.param.essais.label: Trials per task
mesure.mi_test.rappel.pause: at the signal, the cue changes: imagine as soon as it appears
mesure.mi_test.reserve.bon: Valid for this session: Motor Imagery drops with fatigue. Redo the test after a break before taking these settings into your app.
mesure.mi_test.reserve.faible_court: With {emis} answers, this score cannot be told apart from chance ({p}). Redo the test with {long} trials per task before judging.
mesure.mi_test.reserve.faible_long: Even on a long test, this score cannot be told apart from chance ({p}): train again. Take care of the contact of C3, Cz and C4, stay still, and feel the movement instead of imagining it as a picture.
mesure.mi_test.reserve.moyen: Better than chance, but below the comparison score: train again (contact of C3, Cz and C4, and feel the movement instead of imagining it as a picture).
mesure.mi_test.reserve.muet: The model was never sure enough to answer: lower "{prob}" or "{votes}", then redo the test.
mesure.mi_test.reserve.sans_repere: Better than chance. There is no comparison score for these tasks: compare this figure with your next tests.
mesure.mi_test.reserve.silencieux: The model only answers on {taux} of the trials: lower "{prob}" or "{votes}", then redo the test.
mesure.mi_test.summary: The training replayed: your model answers with your settings, and we compare with the cue.
mesure.mi_test.verdict.base: {mot} — over {n} trials (one answer per trial, at the end of the trial), the model answered {emis} times ({taux}). It was right {justes} times out of {emis}, that is {justesse} (likely range: {bas} to {haut} %), for a chance level of {hasard} ({k} tasks). Chance probability of such a score: {p} — {conclusion}. The {silences} trial(s) with no answer count neither as an error nor as REST.
mesure.mi_test.verdict.perdus: ⚠️ {n} more trial(s) were played, but they are missing from the calculation: the engine no longer had them in memory.
mesure.mi_test.verdict.repere: Comparison score with {k} tasks: {repere} (in training, in one person, on this headset).
mesure.mi_test.verdict.sans_repere: No comparison score for these {k} tasks.
mesure.p300_test.briefing.1: This test replays the training, but your model answers: at the end of each round, it makes its selection of a target, and we compare it with the circled target.
mesure.p300_test.briefing.deroule: Sequence: headset settling ({chauffe} s), then the rounds, ~{manche} s each.
mesure.p300_test.chiffres: The right target {justes} times out of {n} rounds: {justesse} (chance: {hasard}).
mesure.p300_test.chiffres.non_mesure: none of the {n} rounds gave a selection (chance: {hasard})
mesure.p300_test.chiffres_sans: The right target {justes} times out of {n} rounds: {justesse} (chance: {hasard}), including {sans} round(s) with no decision.
mesure.p300_test.erreur.trop_peu: {n} round(s) kept: not enough to conclude. Redo the test.
mesure.p300_test.honnetete:
One decision per round: the selection, that is the target your app would have received at the end of the round. The {flashs} flashes of a round do not count as that many trials: the model averages them, and counting them would make the result look ~{facteur} times more precise than it is.
A round with no decision counts as missed: your app would have received nothing.
Comparison points: the training thresholds ({excellent} for EXCELLENT, {utilisable} for USABLE). One or two errors out of six are normal. The P300 depends on your attention: this score describes this session.
mesure.p300_test.label: Test the P300
mesure.p300_test.param.essais.aide: One round = one selection: the window circles a target, flashes the {k}, and the model chooses. Short by default (one round per target). If the result says "not distinguishable from chance", use {long} rounds to decide. At 60 Hz: {durees}.
mesure.p300_test.param.essais.label: Rounds
mesure.p300_test.reserve.bon: Valid for this session: the P300 depends on your attention. Redo the test after a break before taking these settings into your app.
mesure.p300_test.reserve.bon_court: Over {n} rounds, the result stays uncertain: confirm with {long} rounds before taking these settings into your app.
mesure.p300_test.reserve.faible_court: Not distinguishable from chance ({p}): with {n} rounds, we cannot conclude. Redo the test with {long} rounds before judging.
mesure.p300_test.reserve.faible_long: Not distinguishable from chance, even over {n} rounds ({p}): check the contact of Fz, Cz and Pz, look closely at the circled target, then train again.
mesure.p300_test.reserve.moyen: Better than chance, but below the comparison score ({repere}): check the contact of Fz, Cz and Pz and look closely at the circled target, or train again.
mesure.p300_test.reserve.sans_decision: {sans} round(s) out of {n} with no decision: the engine lost data (link, buffer), it is not your model's fault. Check the contact and redo the test.
mesure.p300_test.reserve.sous_seuil: Below the usable threshold ({seuil}): check the contact of Fz, Cz and Pz, look closely at the circled target, then train again.
mesure.p300_test.summary: The training replayed: the window circles one target per round, your model chooses, and we compare.
mesure.p300_test.verdict.base: {mot} — over {n} rounds (one decision per round, never one per flash{epoques}), the chosen target was the circled target {justes} times, that is {justesse} (likely range: {bas} to {haut} %), for a chance level of {hasard} ({k} targets). Chance probability of such a score: {p} — {conclusion}.
mesure.p300_test.verdict.hors_calcul: ⚠️ {n} more round(s) were played but are not counted: their start or end was lost.
mesure.p300_test.verdict.sans_decision: {n} round(s) with no decision (-1) count as no selection, so as missed: your app would have received nothing.
mesure.socle.chauffe: The headset is settling: the measure starts in a moment.
mesure.ssvep_taux.briefing.1: Two questions: when the engine announces a target, is it the right one? And on how many trials does it answer?
mesure.ssvep_taux.briefing.2: A second window flashes the targets and picks one on each trial: look at the one ringed in blue until it changes.
mesure.ssvep_taux.briefing.3: Sequence: headset settling, then {repos} s of rest (look at the central cross, follow no target: the engine measures its resting noise level), then the trials.
mesure.ssvep_taux.briefing.4: Stay still and blink little: a trial that is too jittery is rejected as an artifact, so it is lost.
mesure.ssvep_taux.briefing.5: ⚠️ Do not close the stimulus window during the session: without its end signal, there is no verdict.
mesure.ssvep_taux.chiffres: The engine announced a target in {emis} trials out of {n} ({taux}); nothing in the {muets} others. Of these {emis} announcements, it was right {justes} times: {justesse} (chance: {hasard}).
mesure.ssvep_taux.consigne.essais: Look at the target ringed in blue, in the stimulus window.
mesure.ssvep_taux.consigne.repos: Rest: look at the central cross, follow no target.
mesure.ssvep_taux.erreur.sans_frequence: the stimulus window announced no frequency: the engine does not know what to compare against. The frequencies come from the screen, never from the settings.
mesure.ssvep_taux.erreur.sans_repos: resting noise cannot be measured: {n} usable rest window(s). The SSVEP compares each target to the noise level measured at rest: without rest, no decision. Did the rest happen, or did the window start too late?
mesure.ssvep_taux.erreur.trop_peu: only {n} trial(s): not enough to conclude. With so few trials, the likely range would be wider than the scale (0 to 100 %).
mesure.ssvep_taux.honnetete:
These two figures are read together. On this headset, in one person, the engine was right {ref_justesse} of the time when it announced a target, but it only answered in {ref_emission} of the trials. A long silence between two correct announcements is therefore normal for this mode, not a fault: it prefers to stay silent rather than guess.
What this test does not tell you: nothing about the network path (LSL, clocks, two machines), which must be checked separately, and nothing about tomorrow. From one session to another, results vary by up to a factor of 9 on this headset: this result describes this session, this setup, this person.
These references were measured with another decision rule (other frequencies, artifact rejection on the 8 channels): they are not directly comparable to your figures, only in order of magnitude. This test decides the way the mode does (your frequencies, artifact rejection on the 4 occipital channels), to describe what your application will receive.
mesure.ssvep_taux.label: Test the SSVEP
mesure.ssvep_taux.rappel.essais: still, blink little: a trial that is too jittery is rejected
mesure.ssvep_taux.rappel.repos: the engine measures its resting noise level: following a target would distort it
mesure.ssvep_taux.reserve.bon: Your setup holds up in this session: you can carry it over to your application.
mesure.ssvep_taux.reserve.faible: This score may come from chance ({p}): with so few trials, we cannot conclude. Extend the test, or check the setup.
mesure.ssvep_taux.reserve.moyen: The engine answers fairly often, but it is wrong more often than the reference: raise the "Detection threshold", or check that no target is too close to your alpha peak ("Suggest").
mesure.ssvep_taux.reserve.muet: The engine announced nothing: the resting noise varies too much. Check the occipital contact, then redo the test, staying still at rest.
mesure.ssvep_taux.reserve.silencieux: The engine is right when it answers, but it answers rarely: lower the "Detection threshold", try another set of frequencies ("Suggest"), or redo the rest while staying still.
mesure.ssvep_taux.summary: A window points out the target to look at. The engine counts how often it announces a target, and whether it is right when it does.
mesure.ssvep_taux.verdict.artefacts: {n} trial(s) rejected as artifact (amplitude > {ratio}× rest): they count as "no target announced".
mesure.ssvep_taux.verdict.base: Over {n} trials (one decision per trial, never one per window), the engine announced a target {emis} times ({taux} of trials). It was right {justes} times out of {emis}: {justesse} (likely range: {bas} to {haut} %), against a chance level of {hasard}.
mesure.ssvep_taux.verdict.chauffe: {n} more marker(s) arrived during the headset settling and were discarded: the window started too early.
mesure.ssvep_taux.verdict.faible: This score may come from chance: {justes} correct announcement(s) out of {emis} are not enough to rule it out ({p}). So we cannot conclude that decoding works. This is not proof of the opposite, it is a "we don't know": extend the session, or check the setup.
mesure.ssvep_taux.verdict.marche: Decoding works in this session: this score stands apart from chance ({p}). On this headset, in one person, {ref_justesse} correct answers were obtained, with an answer in {ref_emission} of trials (order of magnitude only: measured with another decision rule).
mesure.ssvep_taux.verdict.muet: The engine announced nothing: this is not a bad score, it is the absence of a score. The resting noise probably varies too much for the threshold to be reached: check the occipital contact, or redo the rest while staying still.
mesure.ssvep_taux.verdict.perdus: ⚠️ {perdus} more trial(s) were played but are missing from the calculation: their signal was no longer in the engine's memory. The calculation covers {n} trials, not the {total} the session played.
